Q: LSTM. Calculating RMSE using inverse_transform A:

Your LSTM is not predicting four features. It is predicting one thing:

Dense(1)

and your target is:

dataY.append(dataset[i + look_back, 0])

you're predicting the first scaled column, which is actually:

24h_volume_usd

not price_usd.

So currently your LSTM is predicting 24h_volume_usd, despite your description saying you're predicting Bitcoin price.

If you want to predict Bitcoin price

For example:

price_scaler = MinMaxScaler(feature_range=(0, 1))

price = data[["price_usd"]].values.astype('float32')
price_scaled = price_scaler.fit_transform(price)

Then use price_scaled as your target.

You can still have your four market variables as input features, but don't use one scaler for both your multi-feature input and your single-feature output if you want easy inverse transformation.

Then:

yhat = model.predict(testX)

yhat_inverse = price_scaler.inverse_transform(yhat)
testY_inverse = price_scaler.inverse_transform(testY.reshape(-1, 1))

rmse = sqrt(mean_squared_error(testY_inverse, yhat_inverse))

That will work because price_scaler was fitted on exactly one column.

If your intended model is:

Use historical BTC market data + Twitter sentiment + Reddit sentiment to predict future BTC price

then the dataset construction needs to be changed.

A more appropriate structure would be something like:

t-2: volume, market_cap, supply, price, twitter, reddit
t-1: volume, market_cap, supply, price, twitter, reddit
t:   volume, market_cap, supply, price, twitter, reddit

                         ↓

                    LSTM

                         ↓

                 predicted price(t+1)

Then your input shape would be:

(samples, look_back, 6)

rather than your current:

(samples, 1, 5)

And there's another subtle point: you're currently doing

trainX = np.reshape(trainX, (trainX.shape[0], 1, trainX.shape[1]))

which gives the LSTM one timestep with 5 features, rather than 3 timesteps.

So despite having look_back = 2, your LSTM isn't really seeing a sequence of 3 timesteps.

Q: How to create/run NestJS server with Bun A:

To create a new NestJS project, make sure you have Bun installed. Open your terminal and run

# Install Bun (if you haven't already)
curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash

# Install NestJS CLI globally
bun add -g @nestjs/cli

to install the tool. Then run

nest new my-nest-app

choose your package manager, and start the development server using

bun run start:dev

Q: Pass TextBox Data to RDLC report A:

You have to set parameter value and pass it to your report:

Dim parReportParam1 As New ReportParameter("parReportParam1", Me.TextBox1.Text)
Me.YourReportViewer.LocalReport.SetParameters(New ReportParameter() {parReportParam1})

In your report you must set textbox value as:

=Parameters!parReportParam1.Value
